question: Which type of rake angle is generally used for milling materials that produce continuous chips?
solution:
The correct answer is __Positive rake.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Positive rake__ angles are widely used in machining processes.
 
• A positive rake angle helps to reduce cutting forces and improve cutting efficiency.
 
• It is particularly effective for materials that produce continuous chips during milling operations.
 
• Using positive rake angles minimizes heat generation and provides a better surface finish.
 
• It allows for smoother chip flow and reduces tool wear in machining processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Zero rake:**

 
 
• Zero rake angles are often used for brittle materials where chip control is not a concern.
 
• They are neutral and do not favor chip flow in any particular direction.
 
 
 
• **Negative rake:**
 
 
• Negative rake angles are preferred for harder materials as they provide strength to the cutting edge.
 
• They can handle higher cutting forces but may generate more heat and wear.
